memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, benign positional vertigo, irritable bowel syndrome.
Patient reports fatigue, occasional flank discomfort, brief spinning episodes on lying down, and intermittent abdominal bloating with altered bowel habit. Examination: BP 138/86, pulse 78, lungs clear, abdomen soft non-tender, no edema. Neurologic: Dix-Hallpike elicits transient torsional nystagmus on right side. Spirometry not indicated. Inhaler technique not applicable. Smoking status: never. ACT not applicable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
telmisartan 40 mg PO OD
 dapagliflozin 10 mg PO OD
 furosemide 20 mg PO OD
 sodium bicarbonate 500 mg PO BD
 betahistine 16 mg PO BD
 meclizine 25 mg PO SOS for vertigo
 mebeverine 135 mg PO BD
 ispaghula husk 5 g PO OD
 loperamide 2 mg PO SOS for diarrhoea
All prescribed for 3 months, review in 8 weeks.

Other electrolytes within normal limits.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, benign positional vertigo, irritable bowel syndrome.
Labs show stable creatinine 1.68, eGFR 38, mild anaemia. Patient reports reduced vertigo frequency after betahistine, occasional abdominal cramping, and mild ankle swelling. Examination: BP 142/88, trace bilateral pedal edema, lungs clear, abdomen benign. No new neurologic signs. Spirometry not indicated. Inhaler technique not applicable. Smoking: never.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Audiometry (pure tone average) performed to rule out concomitant hearing loss in benign positional vertigo.
Results: Right ear 25 dB HL at 500 Hz, 20 dB at 1000 Hz, 22 dB at 2000 Hz, 25 dB at 4000 Hz. Left ear symmetrical. No significant asymmetry; hearing within normal limits for age.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: 'Doctor, I’ve had two brief spinning spells this morning when turning in bed, lasting <30 seconds each. No nausea. My belly feels bloated after lunch and I passed loose stool twice today.'

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Referral to Nephrology, St. John’s Medical Centre, for progressive CKD (eGFR 38, persistent albuminuria) to consider specialist management and possible SGLT2 inhibitor optimisation.
Attach recent labs and medication list.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Nephrology reply: Patient reviewed, CKD stage 3b due to hypertensive nephropathy. Continue telmisartan, dapagliflozin, furosemide, sodium bicarbonate. Add spironolactone 12.5 mg OD pending potassium. Repeat labs in 8 weeks. No urgent intervention needed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3b, benign positional vertigo, irritable bowel syndrome.
Patient asymptomatic for vertigo since last betahistine adjustment, reports occasional bloating but bowel pattern stable. Examination: BP 138/84, trace edema, lungs clear, abdomen soft. Labs show eGFR 36, stable albuminuria, Hb 12.0. Continue current meds, hold spironolactone due to borderline potassium. Inhaler technique not applicable. Smoking: never. Schedule next review in 4 months.
